subject.title: fix(ollama): preserve custom memory provider endpoints

question: After the shared sanitizer is narrowed and current-head runtime proof is supplied, should OpenClaw accept a one-time rebuild of all existing Ollama memory indexes to correct endpoint-scoped cache identity?
rationale: The rebuild is an intentional compatibility cost affecting existing installations, and code review cannot decide whether that upgrade impact is acceptable for the release.

options.title: Accept the corrected identity
options.body: Land the endpoint-aware key after narrowing header sanitization and proving both the rebuild and post-rebuild behavior on the current head.

options.title: Split the shared hardening
options.body: Land an Ollama-only cache-identity fix now and move the cross-adapter sanitizer contract to separate review and compatibility testing.

options.title: Defer the key change
options.body: Keep existing Ollama cache identity until maintainers choose a migration or less disruptive invalidation strategy.

recommendation.title: Accept the corrected identity
recommendation.body: Land the endpoint-aware key after narrowing header sanitization and proving both the rebuild and post-rebuild behavior on the current head.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a repository-wide upgrade and release-compatibility choice rather than an Ollama implementation detail.
